content.text:
I couldn't fix the spec, and I didn't change it. The spec compiler still won't start, the same as on the last step:

```
piton: /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6: version `GLIBC_2.39' not found (required by piton)
```

`/usr/local/bin/piton` hasn't been replaced. It needs glibc 2.39 and this container has 2.36. Every Piton tool runs through that one program: `piton build`, `piton check` and `piton slice`. So I have no way to get an error list, find a broken line, or confirm a fix. I could guess at syntax errors by eye, but I can't build to check them, so I didn't edit anything. For the same reason the understanding file has no constraints in it.

**What I could find:** ten `.pi` files have changed since the reference was last built (Oct 3, 10:06). If the spec does have errors, they're probably in one of these:

- `spec/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.pi` (10:04)
- `spec/scope/spec-build/index.pi` (10:05)
- `spec/scope/container-environment/index.pi` (15:53)
- `spec/scope/project-data/index.pi` (15:53)
- `spec/scope/settings-window/index.pi` (15:53)
- `spec/scope/harness-integration/index.pi` (15:54)
- `spec/scope/prompt-mode/index.pi` (15:54)
- `spec/scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.pi` (15:54)
- `spec/scope/prompt-mode/sending/index.pi` (15:54)
- `spec/scope/open-projects/index.pi` (Oct 2, 19:46)

The 15:53–15:54 batch was saved within about a minute, and `piton` was installed at 16:32, after all of them.

**To get unblocked:**
1. Reinstall `piton` with a build that runs on glibc 2.36: a static or musl build, or one compiled on Debian 12. The other option is moving the container to Debian 13 or Ubuntu 24.04.
2. Check that `piton check` runs. Then send this prompt again and I'll fix whatever errors it reports in those files.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors also still need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings, though this task doesn't use them.
